title: Verifiable attestation webhook for retention & residency controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a webhook contract that emits cryptographically verifiable attestations for: (1) data residency assertions (region of origin/storage), (2) retention lifecycle events (created/retained/expired/archived/deleted), and (3) packaged evidence for audits. The webhook must support both push-based delivery and async retrieval bundles, include signer metadata for non-repudiation, and provide machine-readable TTL/residency fields so downstream partners can automate retention enforcement and cross-region ingestion policies.
acceptance_criteria: Schema v1 published and documented in Confluence with example payloads for residency, retention_state_change, and evidence_bundle events
Outgoing webhook includes signature header (RS256 JWS) and a signed 'delivery_receipt' when requested
Idempotency key in payload and at-least-once delivery semantics with dedupe guidance included
Region scoping fields present: region_code, region_scope, residency_proof_signature
Retention fields present: retention_policy_id, retention_until (ISO8601), retention_action
End-to-end automated test harness that validates signature verification, schema evolution handling, and bulk bundle download
Backward-compatible failover: when webhook target responds 5xx, event is buffered to regional durable queue and retried with exponential backoff
comments: 2026-03-01: Created ticket — initial scope drafted after PM sync (PM: Elena Cho). Asked to define strong non-repudiation for retention transitions.
2026-03-03: Eng design review — proposed JWS-signed payloads with detachable signature header to allow large evidence bundles to be delivered by URL and verified independently.
2026-03-05: Security feedback: recommend KMS-backed signing keys with rotation policy and a key ID (kid) header; ask for threat model writeup before review complete.
2026-03-07: Implementation started — Luca prototyped signature utility and a small test server that validates signatures and dedup logic. PR created: #3842.

2026-03-09: Ops requested that large evidence_bundle events be optionally uploaded to region-anchored object storage and signed object manifest returned in payload to avoid webhook timeouts. Added as follow-up task.
risks: Large evidence bundles could cause webhook timeouts => mitigated by two-phase delivery (manifest + async bundle download)
Cross-region delivery may expose residency metadata if misconfigured => require delivery ACLs and explicit region_scope verification
Signature verification costs at scale (CPU) => recommend offloading verification to a lightweight verifier library and batching receipts where possible
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize schema v1 and Confluence doc; security threat model and KMS signing flow
Week 2: Implement signer utilities in runtime (KMS integration) and webhook dispatcher changes to attach JWS header
Week 3: Build test harness and end-to-end verification job; add retry/backoff and durable regional queue fallback
Week 4: Partner integration runbook for customers to verify signatures and consume evidence bundle URLs; staged rollout behind feature flag
notes: Decision: use RS256 JWS for signatures to be broadly compatible with customer verification stacks; include 'proof' sub-object with signing_key_kid and signer_role
Trade-off: Inline bundles increase delivery simplicity but risk timeouts; opted for signed manifest + URL for large bundles as default for >2MB payloads
Compatibility: Provide a 'simple' simplified webhook payload mode for early-stage customers with only minimal residency/retention fields (no evidence bundle), toggled via subscription parameter
